title: Promoting Armstrong at Frank Palumbo's Philadelphia nightclub
summary: While in advertising in the 1940s, Rose herded Armstrong to radio shows during a Palumbo club week.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Oh, I gotta tell you this, this may be of some interest. During the, the forties, I was in the advertising business. Uh huh. And one of my clients was an outfit headed by Frank Palumbo who was a big nightclub owner in Philadelphia. Right. And at that time he built the largest nightclub in the world, with the biggest bar in the world. It was something like, like it was a, a snake bar, you know, and it was something like three quarters of a mile total. And he was very proud of that. And he used to have big bands come in there on a revolving stage so that there'd be two main bands every, every week. And, uh, so one week we had Louis on one side and, uh, and, uh, I think, Orrin Tucker and Wee Bonnie Baker on the other side. Oh God.

Night and Day. Yeah, that was, uh, oh Johnny, you know. So anyway, uh, I was, I was responsible then to see to it that Louis got on every possible radio disc jockey show in town. Yeah. During that time. Yeah. So I kinda herded him around from one to another and we had a lot of, actually we spent more time talking to each other then, than any other time. And, uh, he was particularly interested in a lot of the people that I was associated with that he knew but he didn't have time to see. You know, people like Ubi and Sissel and Dan Burley, of whom he was very fond, he was the editor of the Amsterdam News, which was the Harlem newspaper. Right. And, uh, he wanted to know what they were all doing and, and he gave me things to tell them, you know, that kind of thing. Uh huh. And so we spent a very happy week doing all this.
